tpms.when: 2011–2013 (sensor in each wheel, no driver reset)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker, and check the spare too.
Drive normally. There is no reset button: the light goes out by itself once the system reads the correct pressures.
If the light is still on after about 10 minutes of driving, recheck the pressures and look for a slow leak or puncture.
tpms.note: A flashing light means a wheel without a working sensor is fitted or the system has a fault; a reset will not clear it. New or replaced sensors have to be registered by a shop with a scan tool.

tpms.when: 2017 (no driver reset; the light clears after driving)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the driver's door jamb sticker.
Drive normally. There is no reset button: the light should go out after a few minutes of driving.
If it stays on, recheck the pressures and look for a slow leak or puncture.
tpms.note: If the light blinks for about a minute and then stays on, the system itself is not working properly and a reset will not clear it. Have it checked by a dealer or tire shop.
